`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]`:
- **Defaults.** It builds the query with `StructuralQuery::new` and asserts `query.limit == None`. An unscoped search returns only `visible.rs` (node `fn[visible]`, excerpt `call()`), so files covered by `.gitignore` and `.git` are not searched. After more files are added, it returns 2 Rust matches, with no limit and complete.
- **Scope narrowing.** `.scope(SourceScope::under("visible.rs"))` returns just the one `visible.rs` match while `another.rs` also exists. Scopes under `hidden.rs`, `skip` and `.git` return no matches. A scope of `..` is rejected with an error.
- **Limit bounds matches.**
  - `.limit(0)` gives 0 matches and an incomplete result.
  - `.limit(1)` on one match gives 1 match and a complete result.
  - `.limit(1)` with two matching Rust files gives 1 match and an incomplete result. This shows the limit applies across files.
  - `None` gives all matches.
- **Language selects the grammar.** The `python` query finds only `script.py`, and `rust` finds only the `.rs` files. `plain-text` gives an unsupported-language error.
- **Rule.** The ast-grep rule object `{rule:{pattern:"call()"}}` is applied, and the excerpt `call()` is asserted.
